newsitem.title: CANADA: US countervail on live Canada hogs zeroes out - CPC.
newsitem.headline: US countervail on live Canada hogs zeroes out - CPC.

text.p: The United States Department of Commerce on Tuesday said it would drop its countervailing duty on live hogs, sows and boars from Canada to zero, the Canadian Pork Council said.

"Today they released their decision and it'll have to be published in the U.S. register and sent to U.S. customs so it'll take effect in a few days," CPC executive secretary Martin Rice told Reuters in an interview.
The countervail rate applied to live hog, sow and boar exports to the U.S. but after Canada cut income stabilization programs to hog producers it wasn't needed, Rice said.

The U.S. Department of Commerce administrative review applies to the Canadian fiscal year between April 1, 1994 and March 31, 1995 when 570,000 live hogs, sows and boars were exported to the U.S., he said.
"Compensation from the U.S. government will go to the exporter of record and it's in the amount of C$1.5 to C$2 million," Rice said.
The countervail rate had been C$0.03 per live kg, he said.
Canada in the last fiscal year exported 2.0 million live hogs, sows and boars, Rice added.
